firmware_v3.title: Upgrade {name} to firmware 3.x
firmware_v3.description:
Firmware 3.x drives the panel from drive data in the configuration. The 2.x configuration of {name} has none, so after the update it draws nothing until that drive data is written. This upgrade does both steps:

1. Check: find the newest 3.x release, connect to {name}, save its configuration to `opendisplay/backups` in your configuration folder, and check that firmware 3.x has drive data for its panel that fits. Nothing is flashed if that fails.
2. After you confirm: flash firmware 3.x over Bluetooth (a few minutes), wait for {name} to restart, then write and verify the drive data.

Keep {name} awake, powered and in range until the upgrade ends. Going back to 2.x needs a manual flash.

firmware_v3_confirm.title: Flash firmware {version} to {name}?
firmware_v3_confirm.description:
The check passed.

- Firmware: {version} (Firmware_Unified, checked against its release manifest)
- Drive data: {panel}
- Configuration after the migration: {size} bytes
- Backup of the 2.x configuration: `{backup}`

The flash takes a few minutes. Do not move {name} out of range or remove its power. If the flash breaks off, {name} may stay in its bootloader: open this upgrade again to retry the flash.

firmware_v3_confirm_untested.title: Flash firmware {version} to {name}?
firmware_v3_confirm_untested.description:
The check passed.

- Firmware: {version} (Firmware_Unified, checked against its release manifest)
- Drive data: {panel}
- Configuration after the migration: {size} bytes
- Backup of the 2.x configuration: `{backup}`

**Untested:** this drive data repeats what firmware 2.x sent to {panel}, but nobody has confirmed yet that it draws correctly with firmware 3.x. If it does not, {name} needs a manual flash back to 2.x and the backup restored.

The flash takes a few minutes. Do not move {name} out of range or remove its power. If the flash breaks off, {name} may stay in its bootloader: open this upgrade again to retry the flash.

The downloaded `{file}` does not match the release manifest (size or SHA-256). Nothing was flashed.

The 2.x configuration of {name} was saved, without its key, WiFi password and FindMy keys, to `{backup}`.
abort.flash_failed:
The flash did not start: {error}. {name} should still run firmware 2.x; start the upgrade again when it is in range.

The 2.x configuration of {name} was saved, without its key, WiFi password and FindMy keys, to `{backup}`.
abort.flash_failed_apploader:
The flash broke off: {error}.

{name} may now be waiting in its bootloader (AppLoader) and not advertising as a display; its configuration is kept. Bring it close and open this upgrade again to retry the flash: Home Assistant flashes a display that sits in the bootloader directly. If Home Assistant was restarted in between, flash it with the OpenDisplay tools instead.

The 2.x configuration of {name} was saved, without its key, WiFi password and FindMy keys, to `{backup}`.
abort.not_back:
Firmware 3.x was flashed, but {name} did not answer on firmware 3.x within {minutes} minutes. When it does, Home Assistant shows the repair "{name} cannot draw its panel" to add its drive data.

The 2.x configuration of {name} was saved, without its key, WiFi password and FindMy keys, to `{backup}`.
abort.still_v2:
The flash ended, but {name} still reports firmware 2.x, so the bootloader did not take the image. Start the upgrade again.

The 2.x configuration of {name} was saved, without its key, WiFi password and FindMy keys, to `{backup}`.
abort.migrate_failed:
Firmware 3.x was flashed, but the drive data was not written: {error}. {name} draws nothing until it is: open the repair "{name} cannot draw its panel" to try again.

The 2.x configuration of {name} was saved, without its key, WiFi password and FindMy keys, to `{backup}`.
abort.firmware_v3_done:
{name} now runs firmware {version} and has the drive data for its panel. Check it with the next upload.

The 2.x configuration of {name} was saved, without its key, WiFi password and FindMy keys, to `{backup}`.

confirm.title: New key for {name}
confirm.description:
{name} was updated from firmware 2.x and still used its old key. Home Assistant replaced it with a new key the display generated, because 2.x keys are often weak or were shared in links.

Other apps that use this display, such as the OpenDisplay website or the CLI, need the new key:

`{key}`

Select **Submit** once you have copied it. Home Assistant already uses the new key.

confirm.title: Add drive data to {name}
confirm.description:
{name} runs firmware 3.0, but its configuration has no drive data for its panel, so it draws nothing. This happens after an update from firmware 2.x, which keeps the old configuration. Uploads to {name} are refused until it is fixed.

Home Assistant writes the drive data for {panel} to the configuration of {name} and keeps everything else. It first saves a backup of the current configuration, without its key, WiFi password and FindMy keys, in `opendisplay/backups` in your configuration folder.

Keep {name} awake and in range. Some panels redraw for about 30 seconds after the write.

confirm_untested.title: Add untested drive data to {name}
confirm_untested.description:
{name} runs firmware 3.0, but its configuration has no drive data for its panel, so it draws nothing. This happens after an update from firmware 2.x, which keeps the old configuration. Uploads to {name} are refused until it is fixed.

Home Assistant writes the drive data for {panel} to the configuration of {name} and keeps everything else. It first saves a backup of the current configuration, without its key, WiFi password and FindMy keys, in `opendisplay/backups` in your configuration folder.

Keep {name} awake and in range. Some panels redraw for about 30 seconds after the write.

**Untested:** this drive data repeats what firmware 2.x sent to {panel}, but nobody has confirmed yet that it draws correctly with firmware 3.0. Check the display after the next upload, and keep the backup.
